name: Tone And Style Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for tone and style, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for tone and style, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting tone and style work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Keep tone and style changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
3. State assumptions about tone and style explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Validate tone and style outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. Prefer the simplest tone and style approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Keep tone and style outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Measure before optimizing any tone and style bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic tone and style advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of tone and style correctness.
- Do not silently drop tone and style edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for tone and style, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
